// xcel-dashboard: Port 5200 is the CONVENTIONAL port, matching vite.config.ts.
One fixed port per dashboard — 5180 Common LMS / 5190 PartnerHub / 5200
XCEL — because all three look alike, so a collision reads as 'the new
dashboard is showing the old project's rows' rather than as an error.
CHANGED 2026-09-21: autoPort is now true. This line used to read 'Do NOT
add autoPort'. That rule was written against the CROSS-dashboard case —
two different repos fighting over one port, the browser still serving
the loser's app. autoPort does not bring that back: the launcher picks a
free port, hands it to vite via PORT (vite.config.ts already reads it)
and opens THAT url, so a preview can never land on a sibling dashboard.
What it fixes is the case the convention never covered — a SECOND
session of THIS repo, usually another git worktree, where 5200 is
already held by an identical xcel-dashboard and strictPort just kills
Nothing here needs 5200 specifically: no OAuth callback, webhook or CORS
origin is pinned to it, and the functions live on the netlify entry
below. `npm run dev` is bare vite with no --port flag, so PORT is the
single source of truth — do not add one. 5200 is still the port you get
configurations.name: xcel-dashboard

// xcel-dashboard-public: The SAME app built as the PUBLIC gateway — VITE_GATEWAY_MODE=public.
It needs its own server because that var is read at BUILD time: vite
inlines every VITE_* at transform, so one dev server cannot serve both
gateways and no URL parameter can switch between them. Without this
entry the public build is only reachable by deploying it, which makes
any change that differs between the two sites — nav sections, the
Demo/Design label in the lockup, the closed routes — unreviewable
VITE_GATEWAY_MODE is set inside the command rather than beside it so it
survives the launcher's own PORT injection, the same shape the netlify
entry below uses. Run it alongside `xcel-dashboard` and the two gateways
configurations.name: xcel-dashboard-public

// xcel-dashboard-netlify: The SAME app, served through `netlify dev` so the Netlify functions and
Blobs stores are reachable — `npm run dev` is plain vite, which serves no
/api/* endpoint at all. Needed to exercise QA Notes and Links, both of
which author into a Blobs store; under the plain dev server they
correctly report the endpoint as unreachable and hide their composers.
Port 8899 rather than netlify's default 8888, so it cannot collide with
a sibling dashboard doing the same thing.
PORT is pinned INSIDE the command on purpose. vite.config.ts reads
process.env.PORT, and the launcher sets it to this entry's own port — so
without it vite binds to 8899 too and every request reaches vite instead
of netlify's proxy. The symptom is /api/* answering 200 with index.html,
which reads as a routing bug in the app rather than as a port collision.
5201, NOT the 5200 vite.config pins. This entry runs a SECOND vite beside
whatever `npm run dev` already has on 5200 — including one from another
git worktree of this same repo, which is the common case when an agent
run is open. strictPort means the loser dies with EADDRINUSE, and the
error is above the prompt where it is easy to miss.
--functions is an ABSOLUTE path, and it is the load-bearing flag when
this runs inside a git worktree. The CLI resolves the functions dir
against the REPOSITORY root, so from a worktree it serves the main
checkout`s netlify/functions/ and a function added here is simply
missing — /api/<new> then 404s (or falls through to the SPA and answers
200 with index.html), which reads as a broken redirect rather than as
the wrong directory. Both endpoints that already exist in main load
fine, which is what makes it convincing.
PATH is set for the same reason the xcel-dashboard entry sets one: the
launcher's shell does not inherit the user's login PATH, so a bare
`netlify` is `command not found` and the pane reports it as the dev
server exiting during startup — which reads as a crash in the app.
netlify-cli installs to npm's global prefix, and this machine's is
$HOME/.local/node, so its bin directory is $HOME/.local/node/bin —
NOT the $HOME/.local/bin the other entry uses, which holds node/npm and
not this. Both are on the front here so either layout works.
If `netlify` is missing entirely: npm install -g netlify-cli
2026-11-21: netlify-cli lives under nvm on this machine ($HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v22.22.2/bin), so that path is on the front too.
configurations.name: xcel-dashboard-netlify

// xcel-dashboard-hub: THE HUB WITH ITS ENDPOINTS LIVE — the entry to use when you need to SEE
the Design or Release section locally (2026-11-18).
Those two sections are derived from `/api/branches`, which plain vite does
not serve at all and which `--offline` cannot answer: the function calls
the Netlify API for the deploy feed and GitHub for the stage/released
facts, and both need the site's own env vars. So this entry differs from
`xcel-dashboard-netlify` in exactly one way — NO `--offline` — which is
what lets the CLI inject the linked site's environment into the function.
⚠ IT NEEDS THE SITE LINKED. `netlify link --id <site id>` once; without it
the CLI has no env to inject and the sections render their 'not
configured' line instead of rows. The id is in `.netlify/state.json`.
Ports: 8900 for netlify, 5203 for the vite it proxies to — one above the
pair the offline entry uses, so both can run at once.
2026-11-21: netlify-cli lives under nvm on this machine ($HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v22.22.2/bin), so that path is on the front too.
configurations.name: xcel-dashboard-hub
